subject: Recap & pricing inputs: PulseHealth hosted API volumes and TPS
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: hannah.lee@pulsehealth.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & pricing inputs: PulseHealth hosted API volumes and TPS

Hi Hannah — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and can move to a short POC / commercial estimate. Please confirm or correct the items below.

Call summary (short):
- Use case: clinical notes summarization + structured extraction for post-visit analytics.
- Integration: queries will come from our backend service (HTTPS -> Redwood hosted API).
- Success metrics: avg latency < 400ms 95th, cost target < $X/1M tokens (see question).

Requested pricing inputs from PulseHealth (items we need to finalize pricing):
1) Expected monthly token volume (total across inference): we discussed a starting band. Can you confirm a realistic range?
2) Target unit economics: target $ per 1M tokens — what internal budget figure should we assume for an initial commercial proposal?
3) Peak TPS (requests/sec) / concurrency at peak: important for latency sizing and burst policy.
4) Any compliance or retention constraints that will affect policy (e.g., HIPAA managed environment, log retention window).

From the call we captured rough numbers (please verify):
- Monthly token estimate: 30M–60M tokens (initial pilot -> Q3 growth)
- Target unit price: you mentioned a target around $1,000–$1,500 per 1M tokens (confirm)
- Peak TPS: ~15–22 TPS during end-of-day batch processing windows
- Compliance: HIPAA required, standard BAAs in procurement form

What Redwood will do next (if the numbers below are confirmed):
- Produce a hosted API commercial sketch with monthly cost at 3 unit price points (conservative/target/discounted committed) and expected SLA impacts.
- Suggest burst & caching strategy to reduce cost on repeat prefixes.
- Propose a 2-week POC test window and a simple evaluation plan (sample traffic, metrics dashboard access).

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Brief_v2.pdf (pricing bands + example unit economics).

Next steps / asks:
- Please reply with confirmed numbers for items 1–4 above by EOD Wed so we can put together a proposal.
- If procurement prefers, attach your purchase/PO form and we’ll start legal intake concurrently.

Thanks again — happy to hop on a 15 min sync if that’s faster.

— Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Brief_v2.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

From: hannah.lee@pulsehealth.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@pulsehealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & pricing inputs: PulseHealth hosted API volumes and TPS

Thanks Laura — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming numbers from our side after internal alignment: 

1) Monthly token volume (expected): 45,000,000 tokens/month for production after pilot. We expect pilot to be ~8–10M tokens over 2 weeks.
2) Budget / target unit economics: Our procurement target is $1,200 per 1M tokens for hosted API (negotiable with commitment).
3) Peak TPS: Observed peaks will be around 18 TPS (mostly 12–15 TPS typical; spikes ~18–20 TPS for hourly batches).
4) Compliance: HIPAA required; we will need a BAA and 90-day log retention for audit purposes.

Additional notes:
- We prefer hosted (no on-prem) to keep infra overhead low. If there are material discounts for 6–12 month committed volume, we’re open to discussing.
- Attached: PulseHealth_Procurement_Form.pdf — use to start SOW/legal intake.

Happy to have Karthik looped for pricing specifics. Looking forward to the POC plan.

Best,
Hannah Lee
Director, Data Products | PulseHealth
hannah.lee@pulsehealth.com
[Attachment: PulseHealth_Procurement_Form.pdf (pdf, 45KB)]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: hannah.lee@pulsehealth.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Recap & pricing inputs: PulseHealth hosted API volumes and TPS

Hi Hannah — Karthik here (pricing lead). Thanks for the clear numbers; that helps a lot. Some quick math and a couple of options to consider:

Baseline math (hosted API simple model):
- If we assume 45M tokens/month and a list price of $1,200 per 1M tokens -> monthly spend ~ $54,000.
- Per-token unit: $1,200 / 1,000,000 = $0.0012 per token.

Discount/commit suggestions we can include in the proposal:
- 6-month commit (10% discount) -> $48,600/mo equivalent.
- 12-month commit (18% discount + extended retention options) -> $44,280/mo equivalent.

Latency sizing note: 18 TPS peak with avg payload size ~600 tokens implies concurrency and KV cache sizing; hosted config with our standard concurrency + caching should meet 95th <400ms for your SLA target. We’ll propose a burst plan for short spikes to 25 TPS.

Commercial proposal items we’ll include in the draft:
- Hosted pricing at three unit tiers (list/target/committed) showing monthly totals and example token-run math.
- SLA and performance notes (95th latency, availability).
- BAA and log retention (90 days) in the draft MSA addenda.
- A 2-week POC plan with sample traffic, dashboard access, and success criteria.

Can you confirm the typical request payload size (median tokens per request)? You’ve mentioned ~600 tokens average; if that’s accurate we’ll size concurrency accordingly.

I’ll get a first-pass proposal over by Thurs EOD. If we land on $1,200/1M as your target, I’ll include the 6/12 month committed scenarios as options.

— Karthik Iyer
Pricing & Solutions | Redwood Inference
[karthik.iyer@redwood.com]

From: hannah.lee@pulsehealth.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Recap & pricing inputs: PulseHealth hosted API volumes and TPS

Karthik / Laura — confirmed: median request payload ~ 520 tokens, 75th pct ~ 900 tokens. Pilot will use a conservative sample set (8–10M tokens).

We’re happy to proceed with the POC; timeline: pilot start week of Mar 1, 2027. Please send the proposal and POC plan. Procurement will review the attached form and follow up on BAA redlines.

Also: small ask on unit economics — if you can show an example where effective cost drops below $1,000/1M via caching and prefix reuse in the POC report, that would accelerate approval on our side.

Hannah
